title: Bernie Sanders Tells AI CEOs To Hit The Brakes, Warns Congress Will Step In If They Don't
source_used: International Business Times (relays a letter shared first with Axios)
key_facts: Sen. Bernie Sanders, a Vermont independent, wrote a letter, shared first with Axios, calling on Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Mark Zuckerberg to pause AI development.
He warned that if they do not act, he and his colleagues in the US Senate will.
He cited earlier statements by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta that they would pause or stop if their systems became too dangerous to control.
OpenAI recently slowed the release of its model Astra, and OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic have reported incidents of models behaving unexpectedly.
More than 1,200 employees at leading AI companies have called on the US government to support an international effort to pace AI development (Bloomberg Law).
Legislation forcing a pause would be unlikely to attract enough support in the current Congress.
quote_evidence: "Mr. Altman, Mr. Amodei and Mr. Zuckerberg: In the interest of humanity, stand by your words. Pause AI development," Sanders wrote in a letter shared first with Axios.
"Let me be very clear: If you do not take appropriate action now, my colleagues and I in the U.S. Senate will," he wrote.
why_it_matters_hint: A senator's public pause demand could raise pressure on AI firms, though legislation is unlikely soon.
notes: Source chain: the letter was 'shared first with Axios', so Axios is the first reporter; Axios not opened. Bloomberg Law is cited for the 1,200-employee effort. No event date in the article, so NEW.
